name: LangShop
summary: Shopify translation and currency app (by Aheadworks) that localises products, themes, checkout, SEO and third-party app content with OpenAI, DeepL Pro or Google Cloud Translation, or with professional agency translators, and adds a geolocated language and currency switcher. Glossary and content rules keep terms consistent. Launched September 2016.
best_for: Shopify merchants selling into several language markets who want machine translation they can correct by hand (glossary rules, brand terms, bulk editing) plus a geolocated language and currency switcher, and whose catalogue and language count fit inside a published tier
skip_if: you sell in one language; or your translations must land in metafields without checking, which is precisely what the recent one-star reviews say is unreliable; or your catalogue is large enough that the tier you need is one of the unlisted ones: check langshop.app/pricing rather than the Shopify listing before you budget
honest_knock: Two things sit awkwardly next to each other in the plan table. The headline promise is 'unlimited words', but every tier caps how many products you may translate and how many languages you may run, so the meter you actually pay is catalogue size. The named engines (OpenAI, DeepL Pro, Google Cloud Translation) now start on Basic at $10 a month (they were a $40 Standard feature when we read the page in September 2026), but dynamic content, metaobjects, third-party app strings and export of your translations still start at Standard. The Shopify listing also understates the ladder: it stops at Advanced and links to 'more pricing plans', while the vendor's pricing page publishes Pro at $120, Enterprise at $250 and Unlimited at $500, and API access, which no listing tier mentions, starts at Pro. The app is old enough to judge (launched 15 September 2016, developer Aheadworks) and most of its 473 reviews are positive (13 October 2026), but 24 of them are one-star, and the recent negative ones are specific rather than vague: a Slovak store reporting that metafield translations ignore both the AI store context and the glossary rules, and a Swedish store of almost three years reporting that products duplicated from another product carry the wrong translation across. If metafields or duplicated products are central to your catalogue, test exactly that during the trial.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month or $100 a year (10 languages, 250 products, unlimited glossary rules)
pricing.notes:
(read 2026-11-17 on apps.shopify.com/langshop and langshop.io/pricing, and in our own test session on 17 November 2026) Basic is $10 a month or $100 a year, Standard $40 or $400, Advanced $75 or $750 and Pro $120 or $1,200. Seven published tiers in all, billed in USD, starting with a Free tier on the listing and on the vendor's page. The Shopify listing shows only the first four and links to more pricing plans; the vendor's own pricing page prices the rest. Free costs nothing and covers one language and 50 products, with limited manual and AI translation, the standard language and currency switcher and multilingual SEO. Basic raises that to ten languages and 250 products, with unlimited glossary rules, the OpenAI, DeepL Pro and Google Cloud engines, unlimited editing of translations, bulk editing and removal of LangShop branding. Standard gives fifteen languages, 2,000 products, automatic sync of 50 new items, the advanced switcher, translation of dynamic content, metaobjects and third-party apps, translation history and export/import. Advanced gives twenty languages, 5,000 products, sync of 125 new items, ten content-exclusion rules and Shopify Flow support. Beyond the listing: Pro adds API access with 10,000 products, sync of 250 and 50 exclusion rules; Enterprise at $250 or $2,500 gives 50,000 products, sync of 1,250, 200 exclusion rules and a customer success manager; Unlimited at $500 or $5,000 lifts products, sync and exclusion rules to unlimited. From Advanced up the language cap stays at twenty. Annual billing is described as two months free, which is the same 17% the listing quotes. Every paid tier now shows a 14-day free trial on both the pricing page and the listing. Between the 10 September and 13 October 2026 readings the bottom of the ladder was loosened at unchanged prices: languages went from one, one, three and five (Free to Advanced) to one, five, ten and twenty, glossary rules went from a cap per tier to unlimited on every paid tier, and the named engines moved down from Standard to Basic. By 17 November 2026 the language caps had moved again at unchanged prices, to ten on Basic and fifteen on Standard, with twenty from Advanced up.

In our own test session on 17 November 2026 on a Shopify development store, the app opened on its plan page and showed no Free card: Basic was the first card, then Standard, Advanced and Pro at the prices above with 10, 15, 20 and 20 languages, and a banner said a development store can test the app and translate up to 50 products for free until it moves to a paid plan. The listing and the vendor's pricing page both still show the Free plan.

compare_with.name: Hextom AI Translate & Currency, EA • Auto Language Translate
compare_with.why: the translation shelf on the Shopify App Store is crowded and the nearest neighbours all publish a free plan, so price is a poor way to choose between them. What separates LangShop is control rather than reach: glossary rules and content rules, translation of dynamic elements (banners, pop-ups, checkout, third-party apps), a professional-agency route for the pages that must be right, and a switcher you can design. What it costs you is that dynamic-content translation only starts at $40 a month, where the free tiers of the alternatives already translate a store after a fashion. Try the cheaper option first if your storefront is mostly static product text; move to LangShop when the wrong translation in a checkout string starts costing orders. (Neighbours read 10 September 2026 on the LangShop listing.)

sessions.what: Our AI assistant ran the test on 21 November 2026 on a Shopify development store with the interface in English. We chose the free plan, machine translated the store's products into German and opened a translated product page in the theme preview. About 2 minutes 50 seconds passed between pressing Install and the finished translation. We paid nothing. German had already been added to the store by Langwill, which we tested just before in the same store.
findings: Install: the Shopify dialog asked for customer device and activity data, staff data and edit access to products, orders, the Online Store, custom data and the Shopify admin.
Development store: a banner said LangShop does not charge until the store moves to a paid plan, and that up to 50 products can be translated free before that.

Free plan: only products (up to 50), payment gateways and navigation could be machine translated. Collections, pages, blogs, legal pages, email templates and theme text showed under "Available on paid plan".
Translation: about 30 seconds after we pressed Translate the dashboard read "125 items translated. 0 items left." The theme preview then showed "Das komplette Snowboard" with German option names.
Switching tip: we ticked "Overwrite existing translations" and LangShop warned there is no undo. It replaced the German product translations that Langwill had made earlier in the same store.
not_tested: Not tested: paid plans. Basic at $100 a year showed as a test charge that would not be billed, but the free plan was enough for our test, so we cancelled that screen.
Not tested: the language and currency switcher, glossary, DeepL or OpenAI engines, paid content such as pages and theme text, professional translation and the public storefront.
